A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SeC framework and SeCVOS benchmark. Their main text, appendices, tables and figures are readable and can be matched across the reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original SeC benchmark results, module and model-size ablations, efficiency measurements, and SeCVOS evaluations, including Ref-SeCVOS in the appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds SeC evaluations on MOSE v2 and M3-VOS, controlled robustness experiments, and additional qualitative results.

M1.justification: The SAM 2.1 backbone, extended memory, sparse keyframe bank, latent SEG-token guidance, scene-adaptive activation, feature fusion and two-stage training remain unchanged. The architecture diagram and explanation of single-pass latent inference clarify the existing procedure rather than establish a new method.

E1.justification: v3 adds MOSE v2 validation and M3-VOS core evaluations, extending coverage to more difficult environmental conditions and objects undergoing substantial morphological or phase changes. The original benchmarks, including the appendix's Ref-SeCVOS task, remain covered.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds TarVIS, UNINEXT and UniVS comparisons on DAVIS and, where reported, YTVOS. The qualitative comparisons also add SAMURAI and SAM2Long alongside SAM 2. The quantitative SeCVOS and Ref-SeCVOS comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New evaluations use the M3-VOS core set with J and MOSE v2 validation with its improved J&Ḟ metric. Appendix C.1 introduces controlled variations in concept-token count, scene detector and incorrect input masks, including forced LVLM activation on every frame for the noise test. Existing training budgets and retained benchmark settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.1 adds tests of one versus multiple concept tokens, alternative scene detectors, and robustness to corrupted guidance. Additional qualitative comparisons and failure cases broaden the analysis. The original online/offline, activation-frequency, module and model-size ablations remain; the sailboat failure case is relocated rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. The added experiments continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 5 newly reports SeC's 53.8 J&Ḟ on MOSE v2 and 67.2 J on M3-VOS core, alongside new comparator entries; Tables 9–10 and Figure 8 add ablation and robustness results. Existing headline results, including 70.0 versus SAM 2.1's 58.2 on SeCVOS, remain unchanged. Table 3 revises MOSE's disappearance rate from 41.5% to 28.8%.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theorems, proofs or mathematical derivations. v3's expanded explanations and references to benchmark-specific metrics do not introduce new mathematical definitions or theoretical results.

C1.justification: The central concept-guided segmentation contribution, SeCVOS contribution and 11.8-point improvement claim remain intact. v3 newly asserts that SeCVOS has the highest disappearance rate among existing VOS benchmarks, whereas v1 only describes its rate as high; this accompanies the changed ranking in Table 3.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations about single-token sufficiency, detector robustness and noise resilience, attributing resilience to feature fusion and noisy training. It removes v1's explicit scene-trigger and short-video limitations while retaining the relocated sailboat explanation. Its new claim of consistently outperforming baselines under noise overstates Figure 8: SeC falls below SAM2Long at five noisy frames and below both baselines at six.

D1.justification: v3 documents the fixed LVLM prompt in Figure 2, clarifies single-pass inference, adds benchmark size and split information in Appendix D, and states checkpoint availability alongside a project-page link. Most training details, including learning rates, batch sizes, data selection and hardware, are retained through relocation to Appendix A.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands coverage of unified video segmentation and recent multimodal reasoning research, including TarVIS, UNINEXT and UniVS, and incorporates the new benchmark literature. The conclusion adds substantive positioning relative to SAM 3, distinguishing SeC's complex-video focus from that work's grounding-oriented concept segmentation.

P1.justification: The abstract and parts of the introduction are rewritten, training details move into Appendix A, and the existing failure discussion moves into the main text. The supplementary sections are substantially reorganized, references move before the appendices, and the broader-impact section is removed. These are substantial structural edits beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned and a dedicated architecture diagram is added. Table 5 gains benchmark columns, comparator rows and best/second-best formatting; qualitative panels gain additional comparator rows. New robustness tables, a noise curve and case-study figures substantially expand the visual presentation, while several existing displays are relocated.

improvement.justification: The architecture diagram, broader benchmark evaluation and targeted robustness tests make the unchanged method easier to understand and better supported beyond v1's existing ablations. These gains are tempered by removing explicit trigger and video-duration caveats and by the new noise-robustness claim that contradicts Figure 8 at five and six noisy frames. The evidence supports a limited net improvement.
